To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supramolecular hybrids formed from pyrenyl-functionalised dendrimers and a Ru4 metallacycle exhibit liquid crystalline behavior.

the association of pyrenyl-containing poly(arylether) dendrimers and the metallacycle [ Ru4(p-cym)4(bpe )2(donq )2][DOS ]4 leads to the formation, in the solid state, of supramolecular dendrimers with a highly segregated multilayered LamSmA mesophase and, in solution, of a multicontinuos thermotropic cubic mesophase.

the supramolecular association between a pyrenyl-functionalised poly(arylether) dendrimer and a metallacyclic ruthenium(II) complex leads to the formation in solution of a host-guest assembly with a multilayer lamellar structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new supramolecular liquid crystals.
the synthesis of new supramolecular dendrimers based on the association of a metallacycle with a pyrene-containing dendrimer.

the development of novel supramolecular materials with a multicomponent structure and with liquid-crystallinity properties, which is an important feature in view of their possible use in optical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the supramolecular liquid crystals reported here can be considered as a unique example of supramolecular hybrids, where the mesogenic properties are the consequence of an interplay between the mesogenic character of the individual components and of the cooperative effect between these components.

the supramolecular dendrimers and their metallacycle complexes exhibit a complex multilamellar and multicontinuous liquid-crystallinity, respectively, which is the result of a delicate balance between the various constitutive components.

the supramolecular dendrimers and their corresponding Ru4-mellacycle adduct display liquid-crystallinity due to their multicomponent nature, which allows them to organize into highly segregated mesophase structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of the pyrenyl dendritic cores with the metallacycle host provides the driving force for the formation of the multilayered LamSmA and Im3̅ m phases.

we are able to design supramolecular liquid crystalline materials by combining the mesogenicity of the dendrimic building blocks with the mesogenicity and self-organization ability of the metallacycles.

supramolecular chemistry can be used to build up new materials that are not easily accessible by conventional synthetic methods, and that the resulting materials can exhibit new and interesting mesomorphic behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multicomponent nature and the complexity of the supramolecular systems can be exploited to design and control the formation of highly structured mesophases with unusual and unprecedented properties.
the supramolecular organization in liquid crystals is not restricted to small molecules, but can be extended to large and complex assemblies, such as the ones described here.

the use of a metallacycle as supramolecular host allows one to obtain a thermotropic cubic liquid-crystallinity for large supramolecular assemblies, even for those that would be expected to display only a smectic mesophase.
